caption:
When do Koreans not book a treatment?
Sometimes because of the skin. More often because of the calendar.

Clinics empty out at fairly predictable times. High summer, because strong sun changes what is sensible to do - that one is about skin. The weeks before wedding season, because everyone books at once - that is a diary. The week around a major holiday, when places are closed, overbooked, or both.

Only one of those three is a medical reason, and all three arrive in your ear as the same sentence: "now is not a good time."

This is an observation about how clinics fill and empty, not a research finding, and it is not a claim about cost. What it gives you is one question.

When you are told to wait, ask which kind of wait it is. If it is the skin, something has to change before it is safe, and you can ask what. If it is the calendar, nothing has to change except the date, and the date is negotiable.

A skin reason has a condition attached. A calendar reason has a date. Both are legitimate. They are just not the same answer.

General education only.

#TreatmentTiming #SunProtection #AestheticConsultation #MedicalAesthetics #KoreanAesthetics
first_comment: Both answers sound identical from the patient's chair, which is the whole problem. Have you ever been told to wait without being told why?
